title: TSMC is seeking chipmaking equipment that doesn't contain Chinese rare-earth magnets
title_bn: TSMC is seeking chipmaking equipment that doesn't contain Chinese rare-earth magnets
author: TechPulse
excerpt: TSMC is reportedly asking equipment suppliers for factory machinery that doesn't use rare-earth components, as the chipmaker seeks to reduce exposure to China’s dominance of critical minerals and permanent magnets.
paragraph1: (Image credit: Getty / Anabelle Chih) TSMC, the world's largest contract chip manufacturer, is seeking alternative machinery without rare-earth components to reduce its dependence on China-dominated materials and avoid disruptions to factory operations caused by the country's export controls. According to a Reuters report on October 22 citing people familiar with the matter, the Taiwanese company has begun approaching its equipment suppliers to explore whether they can provide factory automation equipment equipped with motors that don't require rare-earth materials.

title: BlueStone Slips Into ₹4.4 Cr Loss In Q2, Revenue Jumps 45% YoY
title_bn: BlueStone Slips Into ₹4.4 Cr Loss In Q2, Revenue Jumps 45% YoY
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Omnichannel jewellery retailer BlueStone slipped into the red in the second quarter of FY27, reporting a consolidated net loss of…
paragraph1: SUMMARYBlueStone reported a consolidated net loss of ₹4.4 Cr in Q2 FY27 against a ₹6 Cr profit in the preceding quarter Revenue rose 45% YoY, but higher expenses pushed the jewellery retailer back into the red Its board approved raising up to ₹300 Cr through non-convertible debentures to refinance debt and fund business requirements Omnichannel jewellery retailer Bluestone slipped into the red in the second quarter of FY27, reporting a consolidated net loss of ₹4.4 Cr against a net profit of ₹6 Cr in the preceding quarter. However, its loss narrowed nearly 92% from ₹52.1 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Operating revenue rose 45% to ₹745 Cr from ₹513.6 Cr in Q2 FY26. On a sequential basis, revenue edged up 1.1% from ₹736.8 Cr.
paragraph2: Including other income of ₹24.4 Cr, BlueStone’s total income stood at ₹769.4 Cr during the September quarter. Total expenses increased 34% YoY and 3.7% QoQ to ₹772.4 Cr. BlueStone said its adjusted profit after tax for the quarter stood at ₹19.6 Cr as against an adjusted net loss of ₹26.8 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Its adjusted PAT increased by 42% QoQ.
paragraph3: The company said Q2 FY27 was its fourth consecutive quarter of profitability, adding, “Adjusted PAT shows how our operating performance is reaching the bottom line as the business scales … This demonstrates that the business scale and operating leverage we have spoken about in earlier commentary are now flowing through the bottom line.” It reported ₹53.5 Cr in pre-IndAS EBITDA, a 234% YoY jump. However, its pre-IndAS EBITDA narrowed by around 2.3% on a sequential basis. “Over the past year, a key focus area has been our entry-level price points, where gold price inflation had dislocated our offering. Our redesigned range is now taking more shelf space in our stores, and this quarter we saw early signs of that effort paying off: new customers contributed a larger share of revenue than in the previous quarter, and AOV moderated accordingly,” the company observed in its commentary. Separately, the company’s board approved raising up to ₹300 Cr through non-convertible debentures (NCDs) on a private placement basis, in one or more tranches. The proceeds will be used to refinance a portion of its existing debt and meet capital expenditure, working capital, and general corporate requirements. Store Network Expands Further BlueStone ended September with 379 stores across 146 cities, adding 27 stores over the past three months.
paragraph4: All seven cities it entered during Q2 were in Tier II and III markets. It also called out its investment in its new 3,200 sq ft flagship store in Kolkata. The company noted that it had front-loaded its expansion ahead of the festival season, adding, “While the opportunity remains large, we continue to expand in a calibrated way, both by entering new cities and by adding density in existing ones. We remain on track with our stated distribution objectives for the year.” Its customer base crossed 1 Mn during the quarter, reaching 10.24 Lakh at September-end, up 19.3% YoY. Repeat customers contributed 56.3% of quarterly revenue, compared with 51.4% a year earlier.
paragraph5: On a standalone basis, BlueStone’s same-store sales grew 28% YoY during Q2, while operating revenue increased 43.9% to ₹738.1 Cr. Shares of BlueStone ended the day 2.78% higher at ₹760.45.

title: One easy change makes Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra with RTX Spark a better gaming system
title_bn: One easy change makes Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra with RTX Spark a better gaming system
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra with RTX Spark might not be a gaming laptop first and foremost, but it certainly wants to game. We found that creating a custom 1920x1080-equivalent resolution for its 3:2 screen, missing from its out-of-the-box confi
paragraph1: Nvidia's RTX Spark platform puts local AI inference and content creation first, but Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra really wants to game, too.
paragraph2: The vented keyboard keeps the critical WASD keys cool under load by design, the smooth 120Hz screen can get as bright as 2000 nits with HDR games, and the built-in speakers may be the best I've ever heard on a laptop, period.
paragraph3: There's just one problem: that 3270x2180 screen asks a lot of DLSS upscaling.
paragraph4: The computation that DLSS performs doesn't come for free, and the load increases with higher output resolutions.
paragraph5: This is especially relevant with the Surface Laptop Ultra's high-density panel, which has just 14% fewer pixels than a 16:9 4K display.

title: Zetwerk IPO: Kae Capital, Kalysta Bag 38.3X Returns, Lightspeed Pockets ₹440 Cr
title_bn: Zetwerk IPO: Kae Capital, Kalysta Bag 38.3X Returns, Lightspeed Pockets ₹440 Cr
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Early backers Kae Capital Fund II and Kalysta Capital Fund II bagged 38.3X returns on shares sold through manufacturing company…
paragraph1: SUMMARYKae Capital Fund II and Kalysta Capital Fund II bagged 38.3X returns on shares sold through Zetwerk’s IPO. The offer provided partial exits to investors, with Lightspeed pocketing around ₹440 Cr and Peak XV realising ₹359.3 Cr across their funds. Cofounders Amrit Acharya and Srinath Ramakkrushnan collectively pocketed around ₹423 Cr, while retaining sizeable holdings in the manufacturing company. Early backers Kae Capital Fund II and Kalysta Capital Fund II bagged 38.3X returns on shares sold through manufacturing company Zetwerk’s IPO, emerging among the biggest gainers in its offer for sale (OFS). At ₹151 apiece, the upper end of the IPO price band, the sale price was 38.3 times the two funds’ weighted average acquisition cost of ₹3.94 per share. Kae Capital Fund II pocketed ₹196.3 Cr by selling around 1.3 Cr shares, while Kalysta Capital Fund II received ₹63.3 Cr from the sale of 41.9 Lakh shares. Both investors retain sizeable holdings after the sale. Kae Capital Fund II holds 4.3 Cr shares valued at ₹649.3 Cr at ₹151 apiece, while Kalysta Capital Fund II holds 1.
paragraph2: 4 Cr shares worth ₹211.4 Cr. The payouts come after Zetwerk’s IPO closed with 3.06X subscription, attracting bids for 56.62 Cr shares against 18.50 Cr shares on offer. The company’s shares are scheduled to list on the exchanges tomorrow. Meanwhile, Peak XV and Lightspeed sold shares through multiple investment vehicles, with returns varying across their funds. Peak XV pocketed a combined ₹359.3 Cr through two vehicles – Peak XV Partners Investments V and Peak XV Partners Growth Investments III. Peak XV Partners Investments V sold around 1.8 Cr shares for ₹271.8 Cr, clocking a 23.9X return multiple. It retains 12.2 Cr shares valued at ₹1,842.2 Cr at the IPO price. Peak XV Partners Growth Investments III received ₹87.5 Cr from the sale of around 58 Lakh shares, realising a 3.
paragraph3: 3X return multiple. It retains 4 Cr shares worth ₹604 Cr. Together, the two funds held a 12.1% stake in Zetwerk before the OFS. Lightspeed, which invested through three vehicles, collectively pocketed around ₹440 Cr. Lightspeed Venture Partners Select IV Mauritius sold around 1.4 Cr shares for ₹211.4 Cr, while Lightspeed India Partners II, LLC sold 1.2 Cr shares for ₹181.2 Cr. Lightspeed India Partners III, LLC received ₹47.5 Cr from the sale of 31.5 Lakh shares. Lightspeed India Partners II recorded the highest return multiple among the three vehicles at around 10.9X. Among other selling investors, Accel clocked a 19.5X return. However, Creovate Innovation sold shares at 0.9X its acquisition cost, taking a loss on the stake sold.
paragraph4: Zetwerk Cofounders Pocket ₹423 Cr Zetwerk cofounders Amrit Acharya and Srinath Ramakkrushnan collectively pocketed around ₹423 Cr through the OFS, selling approximately 1.4 Cr shares each for ₹211.4 Cr apiece. Following the sale, Acharya retains 10.1 Cr shares worth ₹1,525.1 Cr at the IPO price, while Ramakkrushnan retains 11.4 Cr shares valued at ₹1,721.4 Cr. Cofounders Rahul Sharma, Vishal Chaudhary, and Ankit Fatehpuria also sold shares through the OFS. The RHP categorised the three under “individual selling shareholders”. Sharma and Chaudhary each pocketed around ₹26 Cr by selling approximately 17.2 Lakh shares, while Fatehpuria received ₹34.3 Cr from the sale of 22.7 Lakh shares. The shareholder payouts formed part of Zetwerk’s ₹5,012.3 Cr IPO, comprising a fresh issue of ₹2,830 Cr and an OFS of up to 14.45 Cr shares worth ₹2,182.3 Cr at the upper end of the price band. Founded in 2018, Zetwerk operates a manufacturing platform serving businesses across industrial and consumer goods categories.
paragraph5: It combines capacity from third-party suppliers and its own facilities to manage manufacturing orders across sectors including renewable energy, consumer electronics, aerospace, defence, oil and gas, and industrial automation. Ahead of the issue, Zetwerk raised ₹2,251.2 Cr from anchor investors. Domestic mutual funds, including SBI Mutual Fund and ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, accounted for around 46% of the anchor book. Global investors, including Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, and Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, also participated. On the financial front, Zetwerk’s operating revenue from continuing operations rose 55.4% to ₹4,117.9 Cr in Q1 FY27 from ₹2,649.4 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Its total net loss narrowed 46.4% to ₹733 Cr from ₹1,368.5 Cr. Of the latest quarterly loss, ₹668.9 Cr came from discontinued operations, while continuing operations accounted for ₹64.1 Cr. The year-ago quarter included ₹803.2 Cr in exceptional charges from continuing operations and the ₹453 Cr impairment charge in the discontinued business.

title: Ola Electric Rights Issue: Motilal Oswal, Calliope Apply For 2.39 Cr Shares
title_bn: Ola Electric Rights Issue: Motilal Oswal, Calliope Apply For 2.39 Cr Shares
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Motilal Oswal Financial Services and Calliope Capital Advisors have applied for a combined 2.39 Cr shares in Ola Electric’s ₹1,000…
paragraph1: SUMMARYMotilal Oswal Financial Services and Calliope Capital Advisors applied for a combined 2.39 Cr shares on the opening day of Ola Electric’s rights issue. Both investors exercised the full rights entitlements transferred to them by promoter group entities ANI Technologies and Indus Trust. The ₹999.74 Cr issue closes on October 30, with proceeds earmarked for debt repayment, organic growth, and general corporate purposes. Motilal Oswal Financial Services and Calliope Capital Advisors have applied for a combined 2.39 Cr shares in Ola Electric’s ₹1,000 Cr rights issue against entitlements transferred by two promoter group entities. The electric two-wheeler maker said in an exchange filing that Motilal Oswal Financial Services applied for 1.28 Cr shares against rights entitlements renounced by ANI Technologies.
paragraph2: Calliope Capital Advisors applied for another 1.10 Cr shares against entitlements transferred by Indus Trust. Calliope Capital Advisors LLP is an investment vehicle owned by Navin Agarwal, group MD of Motilal Oswal Financial Services. Both investors submitted their applications before 11:00 IST on the opening day of the issue, covering the full entitlements transferred to them. Renouncing a rights entitlement means transferring the right to subscribe to new shares to another investor. ANI Technologies, which operates the Ola Cabs business, and Indus Trust held 3.47% and 2.98% stake, respectively, in Ola Electric as of June 30, according to the company’s letter of offer. Ankush Aggarwal, brother of founder Bhavish Aggarwal, serves as the trustee of Indus Trust.
paragraph3: Meanwhile, CMD Bhavish has committed to subscribing to his full rights entitlement. Promoter group members have also committed to subscribing to their entitlements or transferring them within the permitted categories, including to specified investors. Earlier this month, Aggarwal pledged a 4.32% stake in Ola Electric to fund his participation in the rights issue. Another Round Of Fundraising The rights issue, which closes on October 30, comprises up to 37.03 Cr partly paid-up shares priced at ₹27 apiece. Investors must pay ₹16.20 per share on application and the remaining ₹10.80 through a subsequent call.
paragraph4: Ola Electric plans to allocate ₹350 Cr towards repaying or prepaying borrowings, including accrued interest and applicable prepayment penalties, and ₹400 Cr towards organic growth. The remaining net proceeds will fund general corporate purposes. The fundraise follows the company’s ₹780.24 Cr qualified institutional placement (QIP) in June, with some proceeds from earlier capital raises yet to be deployed. As of September 20, 2026, ₹139.21 Cr of IPO proceeds allocated towards debt repayment, organic growth, and general corporate purposes remained unutilised. Another ₹190.77 Cr from the QIP remained unutilised across these common objects, according to the letter of offer. The fundraise comes at a time when Ola Electric is stepping up investments in its battery cell manufacturing and battery energy storage system businesses.
paragraph5: On the financial front, its consolidated net loss narrowed 22% YoY to ₹336 Cr in Q1 FY27. However, operating revenue plunged 45% YoY to ₹455 Cr. Sequentially, revenue rose 72% from ₹265 Cr, while loss narrowed from ₹500 Cr. Shares of Ola Electric ended today’s trading session 3.21% lower at ₹31.94 apiece on the BSE.

title: Manufacturing Startups To Watch: 5 Startups That Caught Our Eye In October
title_bn: Manufacturing Startups To Watch: 5 Startups That Caught Our Eye In October
author: TechPulse
excerpt: India’s manufacturing story is moving beyond assembling finished products. Startups are developing specialised components, materials and engineering systems that power…
paragraph1: India’s manufacturing story is moving beyond assembling finished products. Startups are developing specialised components, materials and engineering systems that power industries ranging from electric mobility and aerospace to energy storage and computing infrastructure. The semiconductor industry offers one indication of this shift. At SEMICON India 2026 in September, the government outlined the next phase of the India Semiconductor Mission, spanning chip design, materials, manufacturing equipment, fabrication, advanced packaging and research. The push reflects India’s ambition to build domestic capabilities across the semiconductor value chain. Policy support is also extending to other manufacturing-intensive sectors. On October 13, the Ministry of Heavy Industries extended the bid submission deadline for a programme to establish 10 GWh of advanced chemistry cell manufacturing capacity for grid-scale energy storage. The initiative is part of the government’s effort to strengthen domestic battery manufacturing. These developments are creating opportunities for startups building real technologies behind industrial growth. However, developing a promising technology is only the starting point. Startups must validate their products, establish reliable production processes and translate engineering capabilities into commercially viable businesses. Against this backdrop, Inc42 is back with the October edition of its ‘Five Manufacturing Startups To Watch’. This edition features Nautical Wings Aerospace, Magron Novus, NuSynth, Refroid and Xbattery Energy, five startups working across aerospace propulsion, electric motorcycles, chemical process innovation, data centre cooling and battery management systems.
paragraph2: With that said, here are the five manufacturing startups that caught our eye in October. Editor’s Note: This list is not a ranking. It is a curated selection of manufacturing startups that have stood out to the Inc42 editorial team this month. Nautical Wings Aerospace | Developing Electric Propulsion Mechanism For Aircraft Aircraft propulsion systems must balance power, efficiency and reliability against strict constraints on weight and operating conditions. As electric aviation and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) evolve, developing propulsion systems suited to these requirements could open up opportunities for specialised aerospace manufacturers. Bengaluru-based Nautical Wings Aerospace is developing electric propulsion systems, motors and composite components for aircraft and UAVs. Founded in 2020, the startup also offers custom engineering capabilities for aviation applications. Its product portfolio includes fixed-wing UAV propulsion configurations with rotor sizes of up to 120 inches and power outputs of up to 150 kW. The company’s work spans electric motors, propulsion integration and lightweight composite components, bringing several critical elements of aircraft propulsion engineering under one roof. Its focus is on developing indigenous hardware for aviation and unmanned platforms. Nautical Wings operates in India’s emerging electric aviation market, which is projected to grow at a CAGR of 7.8% through 2029. Its progress will depend on validating its systems for specific aircraft applications and establishing repeatable manufacturing processes.
paragraph3: Magron Novus | Fully Forged Carbon Fibre EVs Building an electric motorcycle involves more than replacing a petrol engine with an electric motor. Manufacturers must engineer the powertrain, battery architecture and vehicle controls to deliver the performance riders expect. Bengaluru-based Magron Novus is attempting to bring these elements together through its own technology stack. The startup is developing electric motorcycles and related technologies, including wireless power transfer and connected riding features. Founded in 2022, the startup showcases two platforms: the C-20, designed for everyday riding, and the H-35, aimed at the performance segment. According to the company’s published specifications, the C-20 features a 22.5 kW motor, while the H-35 has a 35 kW motor. Its proprietary technology stack includes the Apex Drive system, battery architecture and vehicle intelligence features. The startup is also developing wireless power transfer technology and a virtual assistant to enhance the charging and riding experience. RECOMMENDED FOR yOU E2Ws command a significant share of India’s booming electric vehicle market, which is poised to reach $132.2 Bn by 2030, according to Inc42’s India’s Electric Vehicle Startup Landscape Report. A healthy uptick in sales supports this market’s rally. In September, total E2W sales stood at 2.
paragraph4: 07 Lakh units, a 12.2% month-on-month increase from 1.84 Lakh units registered in August. Magron’s ability to turn its technology into reliable, manufacturable products and bring its motorcycles to market will determine how it develops in India’s increasingly competitive electric mobility sector. NuSynth | Re-Engineering Chemical Manufacturing Processes Chemical manufacturers often face challenges when developing processes for complex molecules. Existing synthesis routes can involve high material costs, difficult reaction conditions, safety risks or production steps that become harder to control at commercial scale. Improving these processes can therefore be as important as developing new chemical products. Bengaluru-based NuSynth Technologies is a chemical manufacturing startup focused on process innovation for complex chemistry. Founded in 2026, the company aims to redesign chemical synthesis rather than rely solely on incremental improvements to existing methods. Its initial focus areas include pharmaceutical intermediates and electronic chemicals, with the ambition to develop proprietary process technologies for global markets. The startup combines chemical research with an AI-enabled platform that uses experimental data to guide subsequent research and development. By recording experimental outcomes as structured data, the platform aims to prioritise future experiments and accelerate the development and commercial scale-up of chemical processes. NuSynth’s operations include an R&D facility and pilot plant in Mysuru, alongside a Bengaluru facility under development.
paragraph5: The company also reports working with more than 20 manufacturing partners across India, providing a potential route from process development to commercial production. Its services include custom synthesis, process development, scale-up and commercial supply. NuSynth operates in India’s speciality chemicals market, valued at approximately $37 Bn in FY25, according to NITI Aayog’s report on India’s chemical industry. The segment accounts for around 18% of the domestic chemicals industry and includes high-value products used in pharmaceuticals, electronics and other industrial applications. Refroid | Developing Cooling Systems For AI Infrastructure Data centres require cooling systems. As facilities accommodate increasingly intensive workloads, conventional air-cooling approaches can face efficiency and capacity constraints. Liquid cooling offers another route, transferring heat more directly from computing equipment to a cooling system. Hyderabad-based Refroid Technologies is an industrial machinery manufacturer developing cooling solutions for data centres and other mission-critical computing applications. Founded in 2021, the company focuses on liquid cooling technologies for hyperscale facilities, edge computing and high-performance computing environments. Its technology portfolio includes immersion cooling, direct-contact liquid cooling, coolant distribution units and hybrid load banks used in testing environments. These systems are designed to support the thermal management requirements of high-performance computing. Refroid has also highlighted its work on indigenous cooling technologies.

The semiconductor industry offers one indication of this shift. At SEMICON India 2026 in September, the government outlined the next phase of the India Semiconductor Mission, spanning chip design, materials, manufacturing equipment, fabrication, advanced packaging and research. The push reflects India’s ambition to build domestic capabilities across the semiconductor value chain. Policy support is also extending to other manufacturing-intensive sectors. On October 13, the Ministry of Heavy Industries extended the bid submission deadline for a programme to establish 10 GWh of advanced chemistry cell manufacturing capacity for grid-scale energy storage. The initiative is part of the government’s effort to strengthen domestic battery manufacturing. These developments are creating opportunities for startups building real technologies behind industrial growth. However, developing a promising technology is only the starting point. Startups must validate their products, establish reliable production processes and translate engineering capabilities into commercially viable businesses. Against this backdrop, Inc42 is back with the October edition of its ‘Five Manufacturing Startups To Watch’. This edition features Nautical Wings Aerospace, Magron Novus, NuSynth, Refroid and Xbattery Energy, five startups working across aerospace propulsion, electric motorcycles, chemical process innovation, data centre cooling and battery management systems.
bangla_paragraph2: With that said, here are the five manufacturing startups that caught our eye in October. Editor’s Note: This list is not a ranking. It is a curated selection of manufacturing startups that have stood out to the Inc42 editorial team this month. Nautical Wings Aerospace | Developing Electric Propulsion Mechanism For Aircraft Aircraft propulsion systems must balance power, efficiency and reliability against strict constraints on weight and operating conditions. As electric aviation and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) evolve, developing propulsion systems suited to these requirements could open up opportunities for specialised aerospace manufacturers. Bengaluru-based Nautical Wings Aerospace is developing electric propulsion systems, motors and composite components for aircraft and UAVs. Founded in 2020, the startup also offers custom engineering capabilities for aviation applications. Its product portfolio includes fixed-wing UAV propulsion configurations with rotor sizes of up to 120 inches and power outputs of up to 150 kW. The company’s work spans electric motors, propulsion integration and lightweight composite components, bringing several critical elements of aircraft propulsion engineering under one roof. Its focus is on developing indigenous hardware for aviation and unmanned platforms. Nautical Wings operates in India’s emerging electric aviation market, which is projected to grow at a CAGR of 7.8% through 2029. Its progress will depend on validating its systems for specific aircraft applications and establishing repeatable manufacturing processes.
bangla_paragraph3: Magron Novus | Fully Forged Carbon Fibre EVs Building an electric motorcycle involves more than replacing a petrol engine with an electric motor. Manufacturers must engineer the powertrain, battery architecture and vehicle controls to deliver the performance riders expect. Bengaluru-based Magron Novus is attempting to bring these elements together through its own technology stack. The startup is developing electric motorcycles and related technologies, including wireless power transfer and connected riding features. Founded in 2022, the startup showcases two platforms: the C-20, designed for everyday riding, and the H-35, aimed at the performance segment. According to the company’s published specifications, the C-20 features a 22.5 kW motor, while the H-35 has a 35 kW motor. Its proprietary technology stack includes the Apex Drive system, battery architecture and vehicle intelligence features. The startup is also developing wireless power transfer technology and a virtual assistant to enhance the charging and riding experience. RECOMMENDED FOR yOU E2Ws command a significant share of India’s booming electric vehicle market, which is poised to reach $132.2 Bn by 2030, according to Inc42’s India’s Electric Vehicle Startup Landscape Report. A healthy uptick in sales supports this market’s rally. In September, total E2W sales stood at 2.
bangla_paragraph4: 07 Lakh units, a 12.2% month-on-month increase from 1.84 Lakh units registered in August. Magron’s ability to turn its technology into reliable, manufacturable products and bring its motorcycles to market will determine how it develops in India’s increasingly competitive electric mobility sector. NuSynth | Re-Engineering Chemical Manufacturing Processes Chemical manufacturers often face challenges when developing processes for complex molecules. Existing synthesis routes can involve high material costs, difficult reaction conditions, safety risks or production steps that become harder to control at commercial scale. Improving these processes can therefore be as important as developing new chemical products. Bengaluru-based NuSynth Technologies is a chemical manufacturing startup focused on process innovation for complex chemistry. Founded in 2026, the company aims to redesign chemical synthesis rather than rely solely on incremental improvements to existing methods. Its initial focus areas include pharmaceutical intermediates and electronic chemicals, with the ambition to develop proprietary process technologies for global markets. The startup combines chemical research with an AI-enabled platform that uses experimental data to guide subsequent research and development. By recording experimental outcomes as structured data, the platform aims to prioritise future experiments and accelerate the development and commercial scale-up of chemical processes. NuSynth’s operations include an R&D facility and pilot plant in Mysuru, alongside a Bengaluru facility under development.
bangla_paragraph5: The company also reports working with more than 20 manufacturing partners across India, providing a potential route from process development to commercial production. Its services include custom synthesis, process development, scale-up and commercial supply. NuSynth operates in India’s speciality chemicals market, valued at approximately $37 Bn in FY25, according to NITI Aayog’s report on India’s chemical industry. The segment accounts for around 18% of the domestic chemicals industry and includes high-value products used in pharmaceuticals, electronics and other industrial applications. Refroid | Developing Cooling Systems For AI Infrastructure Data centres require cooling systems. As facilities accommodate increasingly intensive workloads, conventional air-cooling approaches can face efficiency and capacity constraints. Liquid cooling offers another route, transferring heat more directly from computing equipment to a cooling system. Hyderabad-based Refroid Technologies is an industrial machinery manufacturer developing cooling solutions for data centres and other mission-critical computing applications. Founded in 2021, the company focuses on liquid cooling technologies for hyperscale facilities, edge computing and high-performance computing environments. Its technology portfolio includes immersion cooling, direct-contact liquid cooling, coolant distribution units and hybrid load banks used in testing environments. These systems are designed to support the thermal management requirements of high-performance computing. Refroid has also highlighted its work on indigenous cooling technologies.

title: WhatsApp, Telegram SIM binding rules from January 1, 2027: Who will be affected in India?
title_bn: WhatsApp, Telegram SIM binding rules from January 1, 2027: Who will be affected in India?
author: TechPulse
excerpt: WhatsApp, Telegram and other messaging apps may have to remain linked to registered, active SIM cards under India's new SIM-binding rules from January 1, 2027. The DoT has set December 31, 2026, as the compliance deadline, aiming to curb cyber fraud
paragraph1: WhatsApp, Telegram and other messaging apps may have to remain linked to registered, active SIM cards under India's new SIM-binding rules from January 1, 2027. The DoT has set December 31, 2026, as the compliance deadline, aiming to curb cyber fraud and the misuse of Indian mobile numbers.WhatsApp, Telegram and other messaging apps may have to remain linked to registered, active SIM cards.(AI generated image for representational purposes only)WhatsApp, Telegram and other messaging apps may face new access restrictions in India as the government prepares to implement SIM-binding rules from January 1, 2027. The Department of Telecom (DoT) has issued guidelines requiring the covered platforms to integrate the accounts with the live SIMs used for registration by December 31, 2026. The rules are to prevent cyber fraud using Indian mobile numbers.Under the new regulation, messaging services should ensure that accounts are associated with the registered SIM card that is installed in the device. This may impact the users of WhatsApp or Telegram over Wi-Fi without their registered SIMs, and those who use more than one device or often change their SIM cards. The DoT issued the directive on November 28, 2025, under the Telecom Cyber Security Rules.
paragraph2: However, the precise impact on individual devices will depend on how platforms implement the requirements.What is SIM binding, and why is the government introducing it?Like the others, most messaging apps will use a one-time SMS code to verify your number. Users are usually able to retain access to their accounts even if they remove or disable the SIM card. SIM binding is designed to overcome this by ensuring the SIM card is activated and in the device.According to the Ministry of Communications, cybercriminals exploit this gap to commit digital fraud, including scams involving callers impersonating government officials. Last year, losses from cyber fraud accounted for more than ₹22,800 crore, the ministry said. The rules will enhance traceability and stop misuse of telecom identifiers, the government says.Which messaging apps are covered by the new rules?
paragraph3: As per the order, the covered apps include WhatsApp, Telegram, Snapchat, Arattai, ShareChat, Josh, JioChat and Signal. The impact on WhatsApp's user base in India, estimated to be in the range of 500 million, could be significant.It is possible that the compliance requirements and their implementation could vary between platforms. According to reports, WhatsApp has now started beta testing SIM binding on Android. How will SIM binding affect WhatsApp Web and other devices? Removing a registered SIM, disabling a number or sending messages from a device without a SIM may disrupt users. Additionally, people who travel overseas often or change their phones frequently or use only Wi-Fi on their tablets may want to make adjustments as well.The DoT has revised another part of the directive. The earlier idea of logging users out of Web sessions every six hours has been removed and replaced with a risk-based logout requirement.
paragraph4: This translates to no more automatic logouts every six hours.What happens if messaging apps fail to comply?Platforms that fail to comply with the requirements may be subject to the provisions of the Telecommunications Act, 2023 and the Telecom Cyber Security Rules, 2024.According to a survey conducted by CUTS International, 80% of consumers and over 60% of small businesses were anticipating disruption due to SIM binding. The DoT also intends to launch an MNV platform to verify phone numbers to ensure that they belong to legitimate users.It's important for users to be aware that it's reported as an operational start date (after the compliance date of December 31, 2026). The rules don't say that all WhatsApp or Telegram accounts will stop functioning on that day. The actual impact will depend on platform compliance and how SIM verification is enforced.About the AuthorPragya Singha RoyPragya is a Technology reporter with over four years of experience in digital media and content writing.
paragraph5: She holds a Master’s degree in Journalism and has covered a wide range of stories spanning space, smartphones, gadgets, artificial intelligence, emerging technologies and the ways technology is transforming everyday life. She focuses on breaking down complex technology and science developments into clear, engaging, and reader-friendly stories, with a keen interest in emerging trends and their real-world impact. Before joining her current newsroom, Pragya worked with News9Live, where she covered the technology beat extensively, reporting on smartphones, consumer technology, AI, space and science, while also contributing to video and visual content. Her experience includes breaking news, explainers, SEO-driven stories, product coverage, interviews, unboxing videos and live event reporting. She has also covered major technology and AI events, giving her experience in both newsroom and on-ground reporting. Beyond journalism, Pragya is an avid gamer and a passionate reader of fiction. She enjoys exploring immersive worlds through games and books, with a particular interest in stories that offer new perspectives, ideas, and experiences.

title: Binny Bansal-Backed ShopOS Launches AI Creative Platform Sloosh For Individuals
title_bn: Binny Bansal-Backed ShopOS Launches AI Creative Platform Sloosh For Individuals
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Binny Bansal-backed AI startup ShopOS has launched Sloosh, a self-service platform that makes the image and video generation technology it…
paragraph1: SUMMARYBinny Bansal-backed ShopOS has launched Sloosh, bringing the AI image and video generation technology it uses for enterprise clients to individual creators and small businesses. With paid plans starting at $19 per month, Sloosh is targeting users who cannot afford ShopOS’ managed enterprise services. ShopOS aims to expand its enterprise customer base to more than 100 brands in India and 40-50 brands in the US over the next year. Binny Bansal-backed AI startup ShopOS has launched Sloosh, a self-service platform that makes the image and video generation technology it uses for enterprise clients available to individual creators and small businesses. Speaking to Inc42, ShopOS cofounder Ajay PV said Sloosh targets creators, designers, photographers, video editors and small businesses who want to generate visual content using AI tools without engaging its enterprise creative team. “ShopOS owns the outcome for mid and large brands. Sloosh goes after a much bigger market: anyone who makes visual content needs creatives every day,” he said.
paragraph2: The platform is being opened to users globally, with paid subscription plans starting at $19 per month. Launched today, the platform operates on a subscription model, with paid plans starting at $19 per month globally. Ajay said the decision to build a self-service product followed interest from smaller brands and individual creators who could not afford ShopOS’ enterprise retainers. “Some of our smaller brands couldn’t afford the retainers and asked us to turn the technology into a product they could use. The idea had been brewing for a while, and over the last three months, we worked on packaging the image and video orchestration engine we had built to generate millions of creative assets for our brands into a product called Sloosh,” the cofounder added. Sloosh brings third-party AI image and video models into a single platform, allowing users to generate content from prompts and templates. It also offers reusable workflows called Spaces and a visual canvas, Spacelab, for building or modifying these workflows.
paragraph3: Spaces allow users to repeat a creative task with different inputs without rebuilding prompts and settings each time. The platform also supports batch generation, enabling users to produce multiple images and videos through the same workflow. Users can also access human creative experts for more complex projects, according to the startup. Sloosh supports connections with AI assistants through model context protocol (MCP), allowing users to request image and video generation from compatible tools. The startup said it is also launching an Adobe After Effects plugin and plans to add more integrations. To attract users, ShopOS plans to work with creators and build communities across markets. Users will also be able to publish and share their Spaces.
paragraph4: Sloosh is currently part of ShopOS, but the team is open to exploring a restructuring depending on the platform’s growth, Ajay said. ShopOS Eyes Global Expansion Founded in 2025 by Sai Krishna V K and Ajay, ShopOS builds AI tools and services for ecommerce brands across catalogue operations, category management, pricing, promotions, recommendations, and marketing. The cofounders previously built augmented reality and AI commerce startup Scapic, which Flipkart acquired in 2020. ShopOS raised $20 Mn from Binny Bansal’s investment vehicle 3STATE Ventures in June last year to develop its products, onboard brand partners, and expand its team. Under its managed services model, ShopOS delivers finished creative assets, with its team reviewing and refining AI-generated content before handing it over to clients. Ajay said the startup currently serves around 30-40 brands in India and a few in the US. It has also secured US contracts worth around $500,000.
paragraph5: Over the next year, ShopOS aims to expand its enterprise customer base to more than 100 brands in India and 40-50 brands in the US. Its clients include Kareena Kapoor-backed Fizzy Globlet, Van Heusen, among others. The startup claims its services have reduced clients’ production budgets by nearly 90%.

title: [Update] TravClan Raises $5 Mn From Flipkart, August One
title_bn: [Update] TravClan Raises $5 Mn From Flipkart, August One
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Update | October 22, 16:51 Delhi-based B2B travel tech startup TravClan has raised a $5 Mn funding round comprising a…
paragraph1: SUMMARYTravClan will use the funding to fuel its team expansion as well as investments in global supply, technology, and destination expansion Flipkart aims to expand its own curated international leisure offerings by tapping into TravClan’s technology and network of over 15,000 travel agents The Walmart-owned ecommerce giant’s investment arm Flipkart Ventures also recently backed AI startups Alive and Keploy Update | October 22, 16:51 Delhi-based B2B travel tech startup TravClan has raised a $5 Mn funding round comprising a mix of equity and debt. While Walmart-owned ecommerce major Flipkart and Singapore-based investment firm August One subscribed to the equity portion of the round, Trifecta Capital provided the debt financing. “The next generation of travel software will not just help sellers search faster. It will increasingly execute work for them. Our ambition is to make TravClan the infrastructure that any travel business can build on instead of having to recreate the entire travel stack itself. This capital allows us to invest aggressively behind that opportunity,” said TravClan CEO and cofounder Arun Bagaria.
paragraph2: Original | October 5, 18:51 Walmart-owned Flipkart picked up a minority stake in Delhi-based B2B travel tech startup TravClan to bolster its international travel offerings, expand holiday packages offered by subsidiaries Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel as well as enhancing on-ground support across. The ecommerce giant also aims to leverage the partnership to expand its own curated international leisure offerings by tapping into TravClan’s technology and partner network. On the other side of the table, the fresh capital infusion will support TravClan’s team expansion in business development, engineering, and destination operations, as well as allow for further investments in global supply, technology, and destination expansion. “Travellers today are looking for more than a flight or hotel booking. They want a holiday that is curated around their interests and supported throughout the journey. TravClan’s supplier network and destination capabilities will help us build that experience across Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel,” said Nishant Verman, Flipkart’s SVP, Corporate Development and Partnerships.
paragraph3: Founded by Arun Bagaria, Chirag Agrawal, and Ashish Thapliyal in 2018, TravClan assists travel agents to build and grow online businesses. It works with over 15,000 travel agents to customise and book real-time packages, hotels, and activities. The startup’s cap table also includes angel investors like Cars24 cofounders Vikram Chopra and Mehul Agrawal and Trip.com’s Travis Katz, as well as institutional investors like Leo Capital. Flipkart’s Diversification Push For Flipkart, the travel tech investment adds on to its push to build out its other business verticals beyond its flagship ecommerce platform. While the company has been eyeing new entries in the food delivery and the event ticketing industry, it has been aggressively doubling down on its quick commerce arm, Flipkart Minutes.
paragraph4: Ahead of its annual Big Billion Days, the ecommerce giant announced that it has expanded its dark store network to nearly 1,200 Flipkart Minutes microfulfillment centres across 150-plus cities. The company is now expected to add another 1,000 dark stores by mid-2027 or the Big Billion Days sale of 2027. In recent years, it has also expanded its in-house Flipkart Travel beyond flight booking services into bus bookings and hotel bookings. Cleartrip, an online travel aggregator which Flipkart acquired in 2021, also later expanded into corporate travel. Besides, Flipkart made some additional investments in AI startups last week. Its investment arm Flipkart Ventures backed Alive, an AI-powered platform for live consumer experiences, and Keploy, a native-AI software testing platform.
paragraph5: To date, Flipkart has made over 20 startup investments via Flipkart Ventures across AI, consumer internet, fintech, e-commerce adjacencies and logistics tech. It claims to support portfolio ventures with strategic mentorship, operational expertise and access to its ecosystem in order to help them scale, besides the capital they get.

paragraph1: SUMMARYSwiggy’s consolidated net loss narrowed 16% YoY to ₹922 Cr in Q2 FY27 but widened 17% from ₹791 Cr in the preceding quarter Instamart’s segment loss increased to ₹764 Cr from ₹651 Cr in Q1 FY27, offsetting an improvement in food delivery profitability Operating revenue grew 36% YoY and 11% QoQ to ₹7,571 Cr, while total expenses rose 30% YoY to ₹8,703 Cr Foodtech major Swiggy reported a consolidated net loss of ₹922 Cr in the September quarter of FY27, narrowing 16% from ₹1,092 Cr in the year-ago quarter. However, its loss widened 17% from ₹791 Cr in the preceding quarter. Operating revenue increased 36% YoY and 11% QoQ to ₹7,571 Cr. Including other income of ₹212 Cr, total income stood at ₹7,783 Cr. Swiggy’s consolidated adjusted EBITDA loss widened to ₹760 Cr from ₹695 Cr a year earlier and ₹651 Cr in Q1 FY27, with higher losses at Instamart and its newer businesses weighing on profitability. Across its consumer-facing businesses, gross order value (GOV) increased 25% YoY to ₹20,793 Cr. Average monthly transacting users rose 21% to 27.8 Mn. Total expenses increased 30% YoY to ₹8,703 Cr. Swiggy’s consolidated cash balance stood at ₹13,662 Cr at the end of September, down ₹705 Cr from the preceding quarter. Instamart Steps Up Investments Ahead Of IOCC Conversion Swiggy’s quick commerce arm Instamart reported operating revenue of ₹1,306 Cr, up 33% YoY and 6% QoQ. Its segment loss widened to ₹764 Cr from ₹739 Cr a year earlier and ₹651 Cr in Q1 FY27.
paragraph2: Adjusted EBITDA loss increased to ₹895 Cr from ₹849 Cr a year earlier and ₹778 Cr in the preceding quarter. Adjusted EBITDA margin improved marginally to -9.7% of GOV from -9.8% in Q1 FY27. Swiggy said it believes Instamart’s adjusted EBITDA losses peaked in Q2 FY27. It expects another quarter of double-digit sequential net order value (NOV) growth in Q3 FY27, alongside an improvement of around 100 basis points in adjusted EBITDA margin. Instamart’s GOV increased 31% YoY and 17% QoQ to ₹9,230 Cr during the September quarter. NOV, which excludes discounts from GOV, rose 35% YoY and 13% QoQ to ₹6,594 Cr. However, its contribution margin deteriorated 82 basis points sequentially to -1% of GOV. Swiggy attributed the decline to targeted pricing investments to reactivate dormant users and encourage repeat purchases, changes in customer and category mix, and the initial costs of new dark stores. The renewed spending follows Instamart’s achievement of contribution breakeven in Q1 FY27, after which Swiggy stepped up investments to accelerate growth. Instamart added 1.
paragraph3: 3 Mn average monthly transacting users sequentially, taking the total to 14.8 Mn. Orders increased 29% YoY to 130.3 Mn, while net average order value rose 4% to ₹506. It also added 69 dark stores during the quarter, taking its network to 1,240 stores across 133 cities. Alongside these investments, Swiggy said Instamart’s transition to an inventory-led model will begin in mid-Q3 FY27 and take two to three quarters to complete. The update follows the earlier shareholder approval to cap foreign ownership at 49.5% on a fully diluted basis, enabling Swiggy’s transition to an Indian-owned and controlled structure. Swiggy said inventory ownership could improve Instamart’s contribution margin by around 80 basis points once fully implemented, while giving it greater control over assortment, pricing, and availability. The company also expects its working capital cycle to improve by eight to 10 days, offsetting the additional investment required to hold inventory on its balance sheet. Food Delivery Posts Records Swiggy’s food delivery business reported operating revenue of ₹2,338 Cr, up 22% YoY. Segment profit increased 39% YoY to ₹349 Cr.
paragraph4: “Our food delivery business delivered its highest ever profits and margins while we continue to unlock new category growth through Toing, our standalone offering for affordable meals,” Swiggy cofounder, MD, and group CEO Sriharsha Majety said. Food delivery GOV increased 18% YoY and 6% QoQ to ₹10,054 Cr. The business posted record adjusted EBITDA of ₹341 Cr, compared with ₹240 Cr a year earlier and ₹292 Cr in Q1 FY27. Its adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 3.4% of GOV from 2.8% a year earlier. Swiggy attributed the improvement to advertising-led monetisation, delivery efficiencies, and operating leverage. Bolt and its ₹99 Store together accounted for more than 25% of food delivery volumes. The company retained its full-year food delivery GOV growth guidance of 18–20%, excluding Toing, after growth exceeded 20% YoY in September. Meanwhile, its affordable meals app Toing, now present in more than 50 cities, continued to attract new and dormant users. Swiggy said two in three new Toing users were either first-time Swiggy users or users who had been inactive for a long time. The company said Toing could help lift combined food delivery marketplace growth to 25-30%.
paragraph5: In some cities, Toing’s order volumes have already reached 20-30% of core food delivery volumes. Swiggy said repeat-user unit economics had turned positive in Toing’s earliest launch cities. However, the offering still requires improvements in monetisation and costs to make it sustainable. It expects Toing’s investment outlay to remain within a limited range in the near term, with spending primarily directed towards customer acquisition and supported by its existing technology and execution infrastructure. Swiggy expects greater clarity on the model’s scalability over the next one to two quarters. Toing remains part of the platform innovations segment, whose adjusted EBITDA loss widened to ₹162 Cr from ₹131 Cr in the preceding quarter. Meanwhile, Swiggy’s out-of-home consumption business, which includes Dineout and Scenes, reported GOV of ₹1,508 Cr, up 35% YoY. It posted adjusted EBITDA of ₹8 Cr, marking its seventh consecutive profitable quarter on this metric. Shares of Swiggy ended today’s trading session 5.01% lower at ₹211.30 apiece on the BSE.

title: Little-known eMudhra set the internet on red alert. What really happened?
title_bn: Little-known eMudhra set the internet on red alert. What really happened?
author: TechPulse
excerpt: India’s only certificate issuer trusted by browsers worldwide, eMudhra, is under scrutiny after a researcher found weak security keys in its website certificates. The company calls it a technical flaw, not a breach.
paragraph1: eMudhra claimed that a technical ‘flaw’ led to the generation of weak security keys and that the company was ‘working to establish the root cause’.SummaryIndia’s only certificate issuer trusted by browsers worldwide, eMudhra, is under scrutiny after a researcher found weak security keys in its website certificates. The company calls it a technical flaw, not a breach.On 21 October, widespread disclosures brought to light a little-known Indian company, eMudhra Ltd. At its heart were digital ‘certificates’, which the company allegedly left unprotected on the internet—thereby making its users highly susceptible to fraud. Compounding this is the fact that eMudhra is the only Indian issuer of digital certificates trusted by websites worldwide. Mint explains the debacle and what it might mean for the internet in India.What is eMudhra, the company behind the controversy?Founded in 2008 by Venkatraman Srinivasan, eMudhra Ltd is a Bengaluru-based company that offers digital identity verification, cybersecurity, paperless work management, and associated services. The company went public on 1 June 2022 in a ₹412.79 crore initial public offering, with 60% of the proceeds from the promoters' sale of shares. In FY26, it reported ₹701.6 crore in operating revenue and ₹110 crore in net profit.
paragraph2: Srinivasan, the founder and executive chairman, holds 17.3% of the company. Other promoters alongside Srinivasan collectively hold 54.4% of the company. Globally, the company has six international subsidiaries in Mauritius, UAE, US, Singapore, the Netherlands and Indonesia. Some popular services that eMudhra offers include digital signatures for India’s income tax and provident fund forms, trusted identity and multi-step verification within companies, and paperless document verification.The other side of eMudhra’s business, which certifies whether a website is secure, is the one that was seemingly compromised here.What brought it to the forefront?On 17 October, an independent cybersecurity researcher disclosed on Mozilla's public, open-source web browser cybersecurity incident tracker that websites using eMudhra’s digital certificates could be compromised.Put very simply, eMudhra is one of a handful of companies registered on the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)’s Controller of Certifying Authorities (CCA) list. Interestingly, it is currently the only company from India that is a recognised digital certificate issuer trusted by most web browsers worldwide, including Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Apple Safari, and Mozilla’s own Firefox.The flaw pertained to eMudhra’s digital certificates themselves. One way websites identify themselves as authentic is through digital certificates, which encrypt a website’s information using complex cryptographic keys—a string of 115 characters generated by digital randomness.
paragraph3: This ‘key’ is so long and comes in so many permutations and combinations that classical computers could take decades to guess just one.Instead of such a complicated key, eMudhra’s digital certificates appeared to show keys that were extremely simple and would allow almost anyone with a basic laptop to spoof, guess and then breach. For instance, when users open a banking website, the site uses a mechanism called Transport Layer Security (TLS) to encrypt the user’s data with a certifying authority’s digital keys, preventing cyber attackers from stealing it.Such an incident, the original cybersecurity report said, revealed a lack of emphasis on security at eMudhra for tasks that could be highly critical and sensitive.Has eMudhra acknowledged its fault?In a statement issued on BSE on 21 October, eMudhra claimed that the weak security keys were generated due to a technical ‘flaw’ and that the company is ‘working to establish the root cause’.On this note, eMudhra further claimed that it had not experienced any cyber breach and remained in full control of its security infrastructure. It also claimed that the global digital certificate business was different from its Indian digital signature business, for which it remains in MeitY’s trusted certifiers list. “The global TLS business runs on infrastructure that is completely separate from the India DSC (digital signature certificate) business. DSC and eSign services in India are running normally,” it further added.For its global clients, eMudhra said it is working to prevent disruptions to critical services worldwide and to fix the certification process.How big an impact has it had?Globally, users may see alerts about data breaches or the suspension of banking services in isolated cases, though no such cases have been reported yet.
paragraph4: MeitY, on this note, issued a statement taking note of the incident, issuing a statement on Wednesday evening that said, “MeitY has taken serious note of the reported incident. A special team has been constituted to investigate the matter.” The nodal ministry, however, claimed that the entire impact falls on eMudhra’s global business division, which MeitY is not responsible for auditing.Independently, eMudhra claimed in its statement on Wednesday morning that it has cleared security audits conducted by all the above-cited web browsers, as required.eMudhra also claimed that the impact on its revenue would be 1%—around ₹7 crore ($750,000), per FY26 earnings. However, it further added that the incident “may have some reputational risks on eMudhra which cannot be quantified.”Since the incident was disclosed, eMudhra’s shares have fallen by 37% as of press time. After hitting a lower circuit on BSE on Wednesday, eMudhra was trading 18.8% lower until press time on Thursday.What does this mean for the future of the internet in India?It is difficult to ascertain if the weak security keys by eMudhra have directly led to any breach. Interestingly, on the same day that eMudhra acknowledged its weak certification keys, India’s largest banker, State Bank of India, published a statement stating that 3,897 of its users had their personally identifiable information disclosed online.“The exposed information reportedly included customers’ registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses, residential addresses, branch and CIF identifiers, lead IDs, and metadata associated with loan/lead records and other related files,” the SBI statement read.
paragraph5:
While the two incidents could not be materially linked, breaches that could lead to SBI’s data being leaked online may occur more frequently if weak encryption keys are used to verify a website—creating scope for attackers to steal sensitive information without being detected.For now, there have been no clearly disclosed, direct breaches resulting from the incident.About the AuthorShouvik DasShouvik has been tracking the rise and shifts of India’s technology ecosystem for over a decade, across print, broadcast and web-first platforms. He's been a tinkerer of machines and PCs since childhood, a habit he was thrilled to convert into his profession. This has led him to fascinating experiences of technologies around the world, which is what keeps him hooked to his job.

Shouvik likes to believe that he is one of the few technology journalists in India who can also code. He has also been writing about the rise of AI well before it became a household name, and has met some of the most fascinating people over the years through his work.

Shouvik writes about AI, Big Tech, data centres, electronics, semiconductors, cybersecurity, gaming, cryptocurrencies, and consumer technologies. He is most fond of the stories he has written during his time here at Mint, for which he also writes 'Transformer', a weekly technology newsletter, and hosts 'Techcetra', a weekly technology podcast.

Outside of work, Shouvik spends most of his time with Pixel, whom he believes is the world's best dog. He is also an avid reader, a toy collector, a gamer and a frequent traveller.

title: Explained: What is PHP? Why govt websites went dark? International advisory issued as AI exposes serious cyber glitch
title_bn: Explained: What is PHP? Why govt websites went dark? International advisory issued as AI exposes serious cyber glitch
author: TechPulse
excerpt: PHP has triggered international advisories and forced websites offline worldwide, marking a new phase in cybersecurity in which increasingly powerful AI can uncover software vulnerabilities that humans have missed for years.
paragraph1: PHP has triggered international advisories and forced websites offline worldwide, marking a new phase in cybersecurity in which increasingly powerful AI can uncover software vulnerabilities that humans have missed for years.An illustration picture shows a padlock in front of binary code on a laptop screen.(AFP)Governments and companies around the world shut down websites on Thursday as they raced to protect themselves against hacking after artificial intelligence uncovered critical flaws in a widely used programming language called PHP.The discovery has triggered international advisories and forced websites to go offline worldwide, marking a new phase in cybersecurity in which increasingly powerful AI can uncover software vulnerabilities that humans have missed for years.What is PHP?PHP, which originally stood for "personal home page" but is now known as "hypertext preprocessor", is a foundational programming language that sits beneath popular web design platforms. It helps run approximately 70 to 75% of all websites globally, spanning from online stores and news outlets to critical government services.
paragraph2: PHP vulnerabilitiesThe current crisis stems from two critical vulnerabilities—CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619—hidden deep within PHP's core engine, specifically in its memory management and error handling.CVE-2026-109618 is an out-of-memory error where PHP can leave partially initialised internal data behind if a request reaches the memory limit at the wrong moment, leading to memory corruption and potential remote code execution.CVE-2026-109619 involves stale global state issues in which a fatal error could leave internal state pointing to memory from a previous request, allowing a later request to use that freed memory for remote code execution.These flaws are considered memory-safety bugs that can allow attackers to access servers without authorisation, steal sensitive data, or execute malicious code, bypassing usernames or passwords entirely.How AI exposed a decade-old flawThe bugs had been hiding in PHP's source code for years. While concerns over out-of-memory errors were raised by a core PHP developer during a 2024 audit, no working exploit was discovered, and the fix was delayed due to the complexity of patching without breaking backward compatibility.The vulnerabilities were finally exposed independently by two cybersecurity entities in August 2026, both utilising advanced artificial intelligence:Ryan Austin, a researcher at the California-based security firm Calif, identified the flaws using OpenAI's GPT-5.
paragraph3: 6 Sol model as part of the "Patch the Planet" project.Google-owned Wiz Research independently found the flaws weeks later, utilising their autonomous AI tool, Wiz Atlas, alongside Google's Gemini 4 Argon and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol.Wiz stated that pre-AI, the manual work required to study failures and refine exploitation techniques would have been difficult to scale, but with AI, this barrier has been removed.Why did government websites go dark?Details of the vulnerabilities leaked online on Tuesday, 20 October, just ahead of PHP's planned emergency security release on Wednesday. This leak fuelled fears that hackers could use AI to quickly exploit the flaws at a massive scale.
paragraph4: To shield themselves, many countries and companies mobilised as a precaution, pulling vulnerable systems offline to prevent attackers from reaching and exploiting the flaw while administrators installed the necessary security patches.International advisories and global impactThe discovery triggered emergency responses, service outages, and strict advisories across the globe:The United States: The White House was informed of the vulnerability. Amazon's security chief reported attempts to exploit flaws in one of its decoy systems on October 17 and warned that the flaws were being "broadly exploited in the wild". The US National Security Agency and the FBI urged organisations to isolate affected systems and take them offline if immediate patching is not feasible.Europe: Governments in Finland and the Netherlands took public-facing national and local government websites offline. The UK’s National Cyber Security Centre advised organisations to check systems for malicious activity and consider taking them offline.Japan: The crisis highlighted the country's struggle with ageing digital infrastructure.
paragraph5: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi urged immediate patching, while the finance and health ministries halted certain webpages. Private entities, including Mizuho Financial Group, ANA Holdings, Japan Airlines, East Japan Railway, and Seven-Eleven Japan, suspended various online services and apps.Asia-Pacific: South Korea raised its private-sector cybersecurity alert level and activated emergency measures.With data showing approximately 1.5 million internet hosts running PHP versions for which no fix is available, experts warn that smaller websites run by individuals and organisations with limited technical resources could face greater risks in the coming weeks.

It helps run approximately 70 to 75% of all websites globally, spanning from online stores and news outlets to critical government services.
bangla_paragraph2: PHP vulnerabilitiesThe current crisis stems from two critical vulnerabilities—CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619—hidden deep within PHP's core engine, specifically in its memory management and error handling.CVE-2026-109618 is an out-of-memory error where PHP can leave partially initialised internal data behind if a request reaches the memory limit at the wrong moment, leading to memory corruption and potential remote code execution.CVE-2026-109619 involves stale global state issues in which a fatal error could leave internal state pointing to memory from a previous request, allowing a later request to use that freed memory for remote code execution.These flaws are considered memory-safety bugs that can allow attackers to access servers without authorisation, steal sensitive data, or execute malicious code, bypassing usernames or passwords entirely.How AI exposed a decade-old flawThe bugs had been hiding in PHP's source code for years. While concerns over out-of-memory errors were raised by a core PHP developer during a 2024 audit, no working exploit was discovered, and the fix was delayed due to the complexity of patching without breaking backward compatibility.The vulnerabilities were finally exposed independently by two cybersecurity entities in August 2026, both utilising advanced artificial intelligence:Ryan Austin, a researcher at the California-based security firm Calif, identified the flaws using OpenAI's GPT-5.
bangla_paragraph3: 6 Sol model as part of the "Patch the Planet" project.Google-owned Wiz Research independently found the flaws weeks later, utilising their autonomous AI tool, Wiz Atlas, alongside Google's Gemini 4 Argon and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol.Wiz stated that pre-AI, the manual work required to study failures and refine exploitation techniques would have been difficult to scale, but with AI, this barrier has been removed.Why did government websites go dark?Details of the vulnerabilities leaked online on Tuesday, 20 October, just ahead of PHP's planned emergency security release on Wednesday. This leak fuelled fears that hackers could use AI to quickly exploit the flaws at a massive scale.
bangla_paragraph4: To shield themselves, many countries and companies mobilised as a precaution, pulling vulnerable systems offline to prevent attackers from reaching and exploiting the flaw while administrators installed the necessary security patches.International advisories and global impactThe discovery triggered emergency responses, service outages, and strict advisories across the globe:The United States: The White House was informed of the vulnerability. Amazon's security chief reported attempts to exploit flaws in one of its decoy systems on October 17 and warned that the flaws were being "broadly exploited in the wild". The US National Security Agency and the FBI urged organisations to isolate affected systems and take them offline if immediate patching is not feasible.Europe: Governments in Finland and the Netherlands took public-facing national and local government websites offline. The UK’s National Cyber Security Centre advised organisations to check systems for malicious activity and consider taking them offline.Japan: The crisis highlighted the country's struggle with ageing digital infrastructure.
bangla_paragraph5: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi urged immediate patching, while the finance and health ministries halted certain webpages. Private entities, including Mizuho Financial Group, ANA Holdings, Japan Airlines, East Japan Railway, and Seven-Eleven Japan, suspended various online services and apps.Asia-Pacific: South Korea raised its private-sector cybersecurity alert level and activated emergency measures.With data showing approximately 1.5 million internet hosts running PHP versions for which no fix is available, experts warn that smaller websites run by individuals and organisations with limited technical resources could face greater risks in the coming weeks.

title: Japanese-Themed Dining Chain Harajuku Tokyo Café Raises $3 Mn
title_bn: Japanese-Themed Dining Chain Harajuku Tokyo Café Raises $3 Mn
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Japanese-themed dining chain Harajuku Tokyo Cafe has raised $3 Mn (around ₹28 Cr) in a pre-Series A funding round led…
paragraph1: SUMMARYHarajuku Tokyo Cafe has raised $3 Mn (around ₹28 Cr) in a pre-Series A funding round led by ZeroW, with participation from Indian Angel Network (IAN) and Samved VC Since raising its seed round of ₹19 Cr in August 2025, Harajuku claims to have doubled both its outlet count and overall revenue The startup will use the fresh capital to expand its outlet network by opening 10 outlets in Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Chandigarh, over the next two quarters Japanese-themed dining chain Harajuku Tokyo Cafe has raised $3 Mn (around ₹28 Cr) in a pre-Series A funding round led by ZeroW, with participation from existing investors Indian Angel Network (IAN) and Samved VC. The round also saw participation from new investors, including Blume Founders Fund, Brijesh Parekh Family Office, Epigamia cofounder Rahul Jain, among others. The startup will use the fresh capital to expand its outlet network by opening 10 outlets in Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Chandigarh, over the next two quarters.
paragraph2: It also plans to operationalise central kitchens in Mumbai and Bengaluru by December 2026. Founded in 2021 by London School Of Economics (LSE) alum Gaurav Kanwar, Harajuku operates Japanese-themed dining outlets in Delhi NCR and Mumbai. It operates a casual dine-in chain, Harajuku Tokyo Cafe, and QSR-chain Harajuku Bakehouse.
paragraph3: Harajuku Bakehouse contributes about a third to the startup’s top line. It claims to have sold more than 1,000 loaves of bread per week on Blinkit in Delhi NCR. Since raising its seed round of ₹19 Cr in August 2025, Harajuku claims to have doubled both its outlet count and overall revenue.
paragraph4: “Our focus has been to build the operational infrastructure required to support consistent quality as we expand. We have invested in centralised kitchens and systems that provide daily visibility into outlet performance, ingredients and costs. This foundation will support our next phase of growth.
paragraph5: We aim to achieve ₹100 Cr in revenue this financial year and build on that momentum in the years ahead,” Kanwar said. The fundraise comes amid the growing popularity of café culture in India, driven by increasing consumer interest in niche and international food offerings. According to the Swiggy-Kearney ‘How India Eats 2025’ report, the country’s food services market is projected to grow from $78 Bn in 2025 to $120-125 Bn by 2030, with the organised segment expected to expand at roughly twice the pace of the unorganised market.
